content:
Quick answer: Appropriate, progressive exercise is a core part of osteoarthritis care and can help strength and daily function. The right programme depends on your symptoms, other conditions and ability.

Start with a manageable level

Begin with short walks, gentle range-of-motion work or low-impact cycling if suitable. Increase duration gradually according to symptoms rather than forcing a fixed target.

Strength and function

Simple sit-to-stands, supported step-ups and resistance-band work can help some people. Choose movements that match the affected joints and use support to reduce falls risk.

Adjust for symptoms

Mild, temporary discomfort may occur, but stop and seek advice if exercise causes significant worsening, new weakness, severe pain or instability. Ask a physiotherapist for a personalised plan.

Important safety advice

Do not start a new exercise programme for a suddenly hot, swollen joint with fever or after a suspected fracture. These symptoms need prompt medical assessment.
